traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Phytolaccaceae, which takes in Petiveriaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate; stipules usually absent, rarely present; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes dioecious; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems usually herbaceous, sometimes woody; flowers solitary, in cymes, in racemes, in spikes or in panicles; flowers actinomorphic; perianth tepals; fruit capsule, berry, samara, nut, aggregate, schizocarp or drupe; stamens 4 to 50; carpels (1-) 4 to 12 (-16). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (s.l., with Petiveriaceae) (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): leaves alternate, opposite or appearing whorled across the broad family; the Petiveriaceae genera in the flora (Petiveria, Rivina, Trichostigma) all alternate (the key's opposite leaves belong to Gisekia). Flora of China Phytolaccaceae: leaves alternate.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of China vol. 5 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=2 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): leaves simple.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): blade margins entire, often undulate.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): blade pinnately veined.

traits.stipules.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): stipules minute or absent (Flora of China: absent or tiny). File kept.

traits.sexual_system.note: Flora of China vol. 5 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=2 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): flowers bisexual or rarely unisexual; rarely dioecious. File kept.

traits.ovary_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): ovaries superior (inferior only in Agdestis, not of this family).

traits.hypanthium.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): flowers hypogynous. File kept.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): herbs, subshrubs, shrubs, trees or vines; File kept (Rivina and Petiveria herbs or subshrubs woody at the base).

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): key: Petiveria in virgate spikelike racemes, Rivina and Trichostigma in racemes; the family's compound dichasia belong to Gisekia and the panicles to Agdestis, neither in Petiveriaceae. Panicle kept as sometimes from the file for genera outside the flora.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): flowers radially symmetric.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): sepals usually persistent, petals absent: one whorl, read as tepals (Flora of China: tepals 4 or 5).

traits.perianth_parts.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): key: Rivina and Trichostigma sepals 4; Flora of China key: Rivina tepals 4. Five belongs to Phytolacca, not this family. Petiveria is 4 as well in other accounts; inferred for the family from its flora genera.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): key: Petiveria achenes; Rivina and Trichostigma berries. Samara kept as sometimes from the file (DELTA's Phytolaccaceae s.l., covering Gallesia and Seguieria, genera not in the floras read).

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): key: Rivina stamens 4, Trichostigma 8-13; the family file's 50 kept as the high extreme from DELTA.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): key: Petiveria ovary 1-carpellate; Rivina and Trichostigma carpel 1. The many-carpellate ovaries (6-12) are Phytolacca's.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Phytolaccaceae (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=10687, read 2026-10-19): sepals usually persistent; Flora of China: tepals persistent.
